topics.topic: Exact grammar and validation rules for path placeholders
questions: What is the exact placeholder grammar and validation rule (allowed characters, repeated placeholders, unmatched braces, literal braces)?

topics.topic: Execution disclosure class when no values/files are named (empty set case)
questions: What class is assigned when that set is empty (e.g., skipped/upstream-failed records, mapped-over-empty-list record, zero-input zero-output execution contexts)?

topics.topic: How `stored_value_bytes_max` is applied for `many` value ports (per element vs whole array vs both)
questions: For `many` value ports, is `stored_value_bytes_max` enforced on each element, on the full JSON array as one value, or on both?

topics.topic: Kernel behavior on startup if recovery of one run fails partway
questions: If recovery of one run fails partway (e.g., store call failure or invocation failure outside normal node outcomes), does startup stop (kernel refuses to open surface) or continue recovering remaining runs and open surface anyway?

topics.topic: Precedence between request-schema unknown-field rejection and specific semantic refusal when callers supply disallowed fields
questions: If a propose-binding request includes `effect_class` (or `idempotency_key_fields`), is that field syntactically allowed and then semantically refused by A08, or rejected earlier as an unknown field by A16 schema validation?

When a caller supplies a computed identity field (e.g., `contract_version_id`) that is not part of the request schema, must refusal be reported as schema/unknown-field or as the specific A01 identity-supplied refusal?

topics.topic: Representation of not-yet-produced flow outputs in a resting run response
questions: When a run is resting, how are not-yet-produced flow outputs represented in the run response: omitted, present with null, or present with a pending marker?

topics.topic: Required strictness of trial-case input/expected_output port-key matching to contract ports
questions: Must authored trial-case inputs and expected_outputs match the contract port sets exactly (no missing or extra ports), or is partial expected output (or extra keys) allowed?

topics.topic: Transport-level criteria for classifying attempt outcome as `not_sent` vs `unknown`
questions: What exact transport signals must implementation use to decide whether the first request byte was written, especially with buffered HTTP clients and TLS handshake/write failures?

topics.topic: Whether filesystem I/O in the exchange directory is allowed under purity/sandbox rules
questions: Are function implementations allowed to perform filesystem I/O in the exchange directory, or must any user-level file open be treated as a sandbox violation to keep "no filesystem beyond its input" literal?
